promptLatex: What is the minimum number of cards that must be drawn from a standard 52-card deck to guarantee that at least 3 cards are from the same suit?
hintLatex: Use the pigeonhole principle. There are 4 holes (suits).
If we draw 2 cards from each suit, that is 8 cards with no suit having 3.
The 9th card must go into one of the 4 suits, making it 3 in that suit.
With 9 cards and 4 suits, by pigeonhole, some suit has at least \lceil 9/4 \rceil = \lceil 2.25 \rceil = 3 cards.
solutionLatex: By the pigeonhole principle, if N objects are placed into k boxes, some box contains at least \lceil N/k \rceil objects.
